title: private-deploy-operator-commissioning-cookbook-2026
author: Marisol Rivera
body:
Summary
-------
This commissioning cookbook describes the step-by-step commissioning, validation, and hardened operator procedures for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It codifies safe handoff steps for field operators, scripted acceptance checks, progressive fault-injection validation, and precise upgrade/rollback decision trees. The goal is to provide an operator-focused, repeatable playbook that preserves customer SLAs while enabling safe upgrades and recovery.

Target audience
---------------
- Field operators and deployment engineers performing first-time commissioning.
- SREs responsible for Day‑2 support and runbook automation.
- Solutions engineers validating customer on-prem or VPC deployments.

Why this doc exists
--------------------
- Many private deploy issues are caused by incomplete commissioning and unvalidated fallback behaviors during network degradation.
- This guide unifies commissioning steps across VPC and on‑prem packages and ensures the runtime fallbacks, KV-cache migration, and operator escape hatches are exercised before customer handoff.

Prerequisites
-------------
- Access: operator SSH keys, service account with deployment:operator role, and KMS/HSM provisioning tokens.
- Services reachable: control-plane-proxy, redwood-operator, runtime-gateway, model-store, kv-sync.
- Test workload: synthetic request generator (redwood-loadgen v2.1+) and model bundle with known hash.
- Tools: kubectl (v1.26+), roperatorctl (v0.9+), systemd on operator node, jq, curl.

Commissioning checklist (quick view)
-----------------------------------
1. Preflight and inventory
   - Validate node inventory and firmware signatures.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM trust chain and certificate expiry dates.
2. Network and routing
   - Verify VPC routing, BGP/peer configuration, and egress policies.
3. Install control plane components
   - Deploy redwood-operator, control-plane-proxy, telemetry-gateway.
4. Bootstrap runtime and models
   - Prime model-store and seed KV caches for sample tenants.
5. Acceptance tests
   - Run synthetic traffic with latency and correctness checks.
6. Fault injection
   - Apply controlled network partitions and validate fallbacks.
7. Handoff
   - Document operator credentials, runbooks, and immediate escalation contacts.

Detailed commissioning procedure
--------------------------------
1) Preflight (operator role)
   - Commands:
     - ssh operator@installer.example.local
     - roperatorctl inventory --output json > /tmp/inventory.json
     - jq '.nodes[] | {hostname, serial, firmware}' /tmp/inventory.json
   - Validate: CPU, GPU, NIC firmware baselines, model-store checksum.

2) KMS and certificates
   - Validate HSM slots and a sample sign/verify operation:
     - roperatorctl kms healthcheck --key-id astra-prod-key
     - curl -sS --fail https://control-plane-proxy:8443/healthz
   - Certificate rotation reminder: set cron for certs-refresh every 45 days.

3) Control plane and operator install
   - Apply manifest (example):
     - kubectl apply -f manifests/control-plane/base.yaml
     - kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-operator -n redwood || exit 1
   - Confirm components:
     - kubectl get pods -n redwood | egrep "operator|proxy|gateway"

4) Runtime priming and KV cache seeding
   - Load a golden model bundle to model-store and mark as staged:
     - roperatorctl model push --file /tmp/golden-v1.tar.gz --name golden-v1 --tag staged
   - Seed KV cache for tenant demo-tenant:
     - roperatorctl kv seed --tenant demo-tenant --prefix "/prefix/sample" --payload-file sample-prefix.json

5) Acceptance tests (automation)
   - Run the acceptance harness:
     - redwood-loadgen --target https://runtime-gateway:443 --scenario basic-chat --concurrency 8 --duration 5m --output ./results.json
   - Validate thresholds (automated):
     - p95_latency_ms < 200
     - request_success_rate >= 99.5%
     - model-response-integrity (checksum match) 100%

Validation matrix and pass criteria
----------------------------------
- Core system health: all control-plane components Running and Ready for >= 5m.
- KV sync lag: < 2s sustained for 1 minute during load.
- Prefix cache hit-rate: >= 60% on synthetic prefix traffic.
- Canary model inference: p95 < 120ms for small inputs.

Failure scenarios and operator recovery flows
------------------------------------------
Scenario A: Control plane API latency spike
1. Detection: alert control-plane-api-p95 > 500ms for 3m.
2. Immediate action:
   - Scale redwood-operator replicas up by +1: kubectl scale deployment/redwood-operator --replicas=3 -n redwood
   - Check CPU/memory/steal: kubectl top pods -n redwood
3. If scaling does not reduce latency in 5m: enable fallback routing to regional proxy (see Routing Failover).
4. Escalation: page eng-private-deployments on-call and include alert runbook snapshot.

Scenario B: KV-sync lag and stale prefix reads
1. Detection: kv-sync-lag > 10s or prefix-cache-miss surge.
2. Recovery steps:
   - Pause model promotions that rely on fresh KV state: roperatorctl model freeze --reason "kv-lag"
   - Trigger kv-sync repair job: kubectl create job kv-sync-repair-$(date +%s) --from=cronjob/kv-sync-repair -n redwood
   - If repair job fails: run a controlled cache flush for affected tenant: roperatorctl kv flush --tenant affected-tenant --prefix '/prefix/problem'

Routing Failover (operator pattern)
----------------------------------
- The platform supports three routing tiers: local-runtime, regional-proxy, and hosted-legacy.
- Failover policy example (operator controlled):
  - If local-runtime p99 latency > 250ms or failure rate > 5% for 2m, switch to regional-proxy for read-only inference.
  - If regional-proxy unavailable, fall back to hosted-legacy with throttle at 25% of normal tokens.

Upgrade and rollback decision matrix
-----------------------------------
- Before upgrade: snapshot control-plane and runtime state (see CLI below).
- Run staged canary on 2% traffic for 30m. If canary meets all checks, proceed to 10% and then bulk.

ASCII table: upgrade/rollback matrix
----------------------------------
| Stage      | Traffic %% | Success criteria                         | Rollback trigger                        | Operator action                   |
|------------|-----------:|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Canary     | 2%         | p95 <= baseline + 20ms, success >= 99%    | any 5m window with success < 98%        | Rollback canary, notify SRE       |
| Ramp       | 10%        | p95 <= baseline + 30ms, kv-lag < 2s      | sustained kv-lag > 5s or error > 2%     | Pause ramp, rollback canary       |
| Bulk       | 100%       | steady-state metrics stable for 60m      | p95 > baseline + 50ms or error > 3%     | Immediate rollback to snapshot tag |

Runbook snippets and useful commands
------------------------------------
- Snapshot control-plane state:
  - roperatorctl snapshot create --output /var/backups/controlplane-snap-$(date +%F-%s).tgz
- Trigger immediate rollback to snapshot:
  - roperatorctl snapshot restore --file /var/backups/controlplane-snap-2026-02-28-158824.tgz --confirm
- Quick cache flush (tenant):
  - roperatorctl kv flush --tenant demo-tenant --prefix '/prefix/test' --dry-run=false
- Force model swap to fallback quantized variant:
  - roperatorctl model swap --tenant demo-tenant --from golden-v2 --to golden-v2-q8 --force --grace-period 30s

Operator safety checks (pre-handoff)
-----------------------------------
- All manifests deployed and validated with immutable tags (no :latest allowed).
- Backup snapshots present in two distinct locations (NFS and S3-compatible endpoint).
- Evidence of a successful canary run: results.json and perf graphs archived to telemetry-s3 (retention 90d).
- Operator competency sign-off: two operators must complete the commissioning checklist and sign the handoff SOP.

SLOs and monitoring thresholds (customer-facing decomposition)
-------------------------------------------------------------
- Inference P95 (per-tenant): target 120ms, objective 200ms, failure when > 500ms.
- Control plane API P95: target 150ms, failure when > 500ms for 3m.
- Request success rate: target 99.9% monthly, operational alert when 99.5% in 10m window.
- KV-sync lag: target < 2s, alert at 10s.

Escalation and ownership
------------------------
- First responder: operator on-call (operator-team-slack #private-ops).
- Secondary: eng-private-deployments on-call rotation (pager duty).
- Tertiary escalation: runtime-engineering (runtime-team@redwood.example.com).

Appendix A: Example systemd unit for roperator agent (field operator)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Operator Agent
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/roperator-agent --config /etc/redwood/agent.yml
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
LimitNOFILE=65536

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Appendix B: Acceptance test YAML snippet
---------------------------------------
scenarios:
  - name: canary-chat
    duration: 30m
    concurrency: 4
    checks:
      - name: p95_latency_ms
        max: 200
      - name: success_rate
        min: 0.995

Appendix C: Troubleshooting checklist for common red flags
----------------------------------------------------------
- High CPU steal on operator host: check underlying hypervisor and consider host reboot during maintenance window.
- Unexpected model inference mismatches: compare model-store artifact SHA with golden manifest and restore if mismatch.
- Persistently failing kv-sync job: capture logs (kubectl logs job/kv-sync-repair-*) and run diagnostic with --verbose.

Contact and feedback
--------------------
If this cookbook misses a scenario or a command fails, create a PR against the confluence page and email eng-private-deployments@redwood.example.com. For emergency escalation, follow the on-call rota documented in eng-sre/runbooks and page the runtime engineering lead.

Related diagrams and artifacts
-----------------------------
- Diagrams: regional-proxy-fallback-sequence.svg (stored in asset-bucket).
- Artifacts: acceptance-results archive and snapshot manifests are required during handoff.
